atoms.a: Who do you think is mostly responsible for managing tourism?

feedback.end: The government can put laws in place that aim to protect their country from the negative effects of tourism.

atoms.b: One example of this is Bhutan, a country in South Asia whose ((++government covenant)) wants to protect their area of the Himalayas from tourists.
They have done this by putting legislation in place that ((++prevents encourages)) mass tourism and conserves the environment.

instruction.text: Drag the words to the gaps to learn about Bhutan’s tourism guidelines.

hint.text: By “high value, low volume”, the government mean that they only want a small amount of tourists, focusing instead on high-quality, sustainable travel.
hint.label: High value, low volume

sound.end: This government follows a policy of high value, low volume.
Tourists must pay a Sustainable Development Fee of $100 for each day that they are in Bhutan.
Tourists must be accompanied by a guide.

feedback.finish: These guidelines minimise the amount of tourists in the country and make sure that they are being educated on the country’s culture and are respecting the environment.

feedback.end: Sustainable tourism is a responsible approach to travel that aims to minimise negative impacts on the environment and local communities.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: There are many ways that tourists can travel more sustainably. Reducing the amount of flights you take is one example, as planes produce much more polluting emissions than other methods of transport.
Tourists can also prevent the loss of culture in areas they travel to by educating themselves on the local traditions, food and language.

Staying in less commercial places, such as small hotels or campsites run by locals, is another example. This ensures that local people receive money from tourists instead of large, international hotel companies.
